The present invention relates to a motor driving apparatus and a home appliance comprising the same. The motor driving apparatus according to an embodiment of the present invention comprises: an inverter which converts a direct current power source of a DC stage capacitor to an alternating current power source and outputs the converted alternating power source to a motor by a switching operation; a DC stage resistance device arranged between the DC stage capacitor and the inverter; and a control unit which controls the inverter on the basis of phase current sampled by means of the DC stage resistance device, wherein the control unit controls the frequency of voltage applied to the motor or the rotation frequency of the motor to be synchronized with the sampling frequency of the phase current sampled via the DC stage resistance device. Accordingly, it is possible to accurately calculate the phase current flowing through the motor by means of the DC stage resistance device.

outputs.L1: The present invention relates to a motor driving apparatus and a home appliance comprising the same. According to an embodiment of the present invention, the motor driving apparatus comprises: an inverter configured to convert direct-current power from a DC-link capacitor into alternating-current power through a switching operation and to output the converted alternating-current power to a motor; a DC-link resistance device disposed between the DC-link capacitor and the inverter; and a control unit configured to control the inverter based on phase current sampled through the DC-link resistance device. The control unit controls the frequency of the voltage applied to the motor or the rotational frequency of the motor such that it is synchronized with the sampling frequency of the phase current sampled through the DC-link resistance device. Accordingly, the phase current flowing through the motor can be accurately calculated using the DC-link resistance device.
outputs.L2: The invention concerns a motor drive device and a household appliance incorporating that device. In one embodiment, the motor drive device includes an inverter that performs switching operations to transform DC power from a DC-link capacitor into AC power and supply the resulting AC power to a motor. The device also includes a DC-link resistor positioned between the DC-link capacitor and the inverter, as well as a controller that regulates the inverter based on phase-current samples obtained through the DC-link resistor. The controller synchronizes either the frequency of the voltage delivered to the motor or the motor’s rotational frequency with the sampling frequency used to acquire the phase current through the DC-link resistor. This configuration enables the phase current flowing in the motor to be calculated accurately using the DC-link resistor.
outputs.L3:
The invention relates to a motor-driving apparatus and a home appliance incorporating the apparatus. The motor-driving apparatus includes an inverter configured to convert direct-current power supplied from a DC-stage capacitor into alternating-current power for driving a motor. This conversion is performed through controlled switching operations within the inverter.

A DC-stage resistance device is disposed between the DC-stage capacitor and the inverter. The resistance device enables sampling of the motor’s phase current by detecting current flowing through the DC stage. A control unit receives the sampled current information and controls the switching operations of the inverter accordingly.

To improve current-detection accuracy, the control unit synchronizes either the frequency of the voltage applied to the motor or the motor’s rotational frequency with the phase-current sampling frequency. This synchronization allows the control unit to calculate the motor’s phase current accurately, thereby supporting stable and precise motor operation.
outputs.L4:
A motor-driving apparatus for a home appliance includes an inverter that converts direct-current power into alternating-current power for driving a motor, a resistor disposed in a DC-link portion of the inverter, and a controller configured to control operation of the inverter. The controller detects a voltage generated across the DC-link resistor and, based on the detected voltage and the switching state of the inverter, calculates the phase currents supplied to the motor.

To improve the accuracy of the phase-current calculation, the controller synchronizes the frequency of the voltage applied to the motor, or the rotational frequency of the motor, with the frequency at which the current is sampled through the DC-link resistor. This synchronization allows current sampling to occur at suitable and repeatable points in the motor-driving cycle. As a result, the controller can more reliably reconstruct the individual motor phase currents from the DC-link current, even though only a single current-sensing resistor is used.

The calculated phase-current values may then be used to regulate inverter switching, motor speed, torque, and other operating conditions. By reducing current-detection errors and avoiding unstable sampling intervals, the apparatus provides more precise and dependable motor control. It can also reduce the need for separate current sensors for each motor phase, thereby simplifying the circuit, lowering cost, and improving the reliability and efficiency of motor-driven home appliances.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent abstract for a motor driving apparatus that uses a DC-link shunt resistor to sample phase current and synchronizes the motor voltage or rotational frequency with the current-sampling frequency.
counterfactuals.output: A motor driving apparatus includes an inverter configured to convert DC-link power into multiphase AC power for driving a motor, a shunt resistor disposed in a DC link of the inverter, a current-sampling circuit configured to sample a voltage across the shunt resistor and determine a phase current of the motor, and a controller configured to control switching of the inverter. The controller synchronizes at least one of a motor voltage frequency and a rotational frequency of the motor with a current-sampling frequency of the current-sampling circuit. The synchronization may be performed by adjusting an inverter switching pattern, an output-voltage command, a motor-speed command, or a sampling timing such that a predetermined relationship is maintained between the current-sampling frequency and the motor voltage or rotational frequency. Accordingly, phase-current reconstruction using the DC-link shunt resistor is stabilized, thereby reducing beat interference and sampling error and improving motor-control performance.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an invention for accurately calculating motor phase current in a home appliance, including an inverter, a DC stage capacitor, a DC stage resistance device, and a controller.
counterfactuals.output:
An invention for accurately determining motor phase current in a home appliance comprises:

- an **inverter** that converts DC-stage power into multiphase power for driving a motor;
- a **DC-stage capacitor** connected across the DC bus to smooth its voltage;
- a **DC-stage resistance device**, such as a shunt resistor, arranged to provide a signal representative of DC-stage current; and
- a **controller** synchronized with the inverter’s pulse-width-modulation switching.

The controller measures the voltage across the resistance device and the DC-bus voltage at selected switching instants. It determines the current associated with the capacitor, for example from the capacitor value and the rate of change of bus voltage, and compensates the measured DC-stage current for capacitor charging, discharging, leakage, and switching effects. Using the inverter switching state, the controller then maps the compensated DC current to the corresponding motor phase or phases. Measurements from multiple switching states may be combined or interpolated to reconstruct all phase currents.

By accounting for current diverted through the DC-stage capacitor and by sampling when the inverter switching state is known and stable, the invention calculates motor phase current more accurately than a basic single-shunt method. It can therefore improve torque control, efficiency, overload protection, and fault detection while avoiding separate current sensors in every motor phase.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a formal patent-style summary of a motor control system in which an inverter supplies AC power to a motor and the controller synchronizes motor operation with DC-link current sampling.
counterfactuals.output:
A motor control system includes an inverter configured to convert direct-current power supplied through a DC link into alternating-current power for driving an electric motor, a current sensor configured to detect a current flowing through the DC link, and a controller operatively coupled to the inverter and the current sensor. The controller generates switching commands for a plurality of switching elements of the inverter and controls operation of the motor based at least in part on sampled values of the DC-link current.

The controller synchronizes sampling of the DC-link current with switching operation of the inverter. In particular, the controller may determine one or more sampling intervals based on a pulse-width-modulation pattern, switching states of the inverter, motor electrical position, commanded voltage, or combinations thereof. The sampling intervals may be selected to avoid switching transients and to provide a measurable DC-link current corresponding to one or more motor phase currents. The controller triggers acquisition of the DC-link current during the selected intervals and may reconstruct or estimate the motor phase currents from the acquired samples and the associated inverter switching states.

When a suitable sampling interval is unavailable or has insufficient duration, the controller may modify the switching timing while maintaining a desired average output voltage, defer sampling, select an alternative sampling instant, or estimate current using previously sampled values or a motor model. The reconstructed or estimated phase-current information may be used to regulate motor torque, speed, position, or flux and to detect an overcurrent or other operating condition. Synchronizing motor operation with DC-link current sampling thereby enables current-based motor control using a reduced number of current sensors while improving sampling reliability in the presence of inverter switching.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.output: A motor driving apparatus and a home appliance including the same are disclosed. The motor driving apparatus includes a converter configured to convert input power into direct-current (DC) power, a DC capacitor configured to smooth the DC power, an inverter configured to convert the smoothed DC power into alternating-current power for driving a motor, a resistor electrically connected between the DC capacitor and the inverter, a current detector configured to sample a voltage across the resistor, and a controller configured to determine at least one phase current of the motor based on the sampled voltage and a switching state of the inverter. The controller controls switching elements of the inverter according to the determined phase current and a motor operation command, thereby providing accurate motor current control using a single DC-link current-sensing resistor while reducing circuit complexity and manufacturing cost.
